title: Elizondo won't confirm or deny Immaculate Constellation before Congress

tellings.quote: and if you even watch him in front of Congress, you know, uh, in September of 24, he's saying, "I can't confirm or deny being read into, you know, Immaculate Constellation."

tellings.page: Questioning by Ms. Mace, second round
tellings.quote: Ma'am, I would not be authorized to confirm nor deny the existence of any ongoing or past program, especially as it relates to a special access program, either by name or trigraph.

plain: Asked by Congress whether he had been cleared into a secret UFO program called Immaculate Constellation, a former Pentagon official named Luis Elizondo would neither confirm nor deny it. The program's name had just come out in an anonymous report handed to Congress. Michels brings this up himself, saying that if you watch Elizondo in front of Congress he says, in effect, "I can't confirm or deny being read into" it, that is, given the clearance to know about it. Michels places this in September 2024. The official record, from the House Oversight Committee hearing Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena: Exposing the Truth, puts it on 13 November 2024. There Rep. Nancy Mace asked, "were you read in to the Immaculate Constellation program?" Elizondo answered: "Ma'am, I would not be authorized to confirm nor deny the existence of any ongoing or past program, especially as it relates to a special access program, either by name or trigraph", a trigraph being a program's three-letter code. Michels tells it because, to him, the answer suggests the program might be real.

discussion.by: Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena: Exposing the Truth
discussion.text: Luis Elizondo gave this answer to Rep. Nancy Mace's question "were you read in to the Immaculate Constellation program?" at the House Oversight hearing of 13 November 2024; Jesse Michels places it in September 2024.
